title: Multi-GPU KV cache memory sharding strategy for tensor/pipeline parallel models
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Design and implement a robust multi-GPU memory sharding strategy for the KV cache that works correctly and efficiently in presence of tensor parallel (TP) and pipeline parallel (PP) model partitions, while preserving continuous batching behavior and minimizing host<->device transfers. Background: With bigger context lengths and larger steady-state workloads, KV cache memory is a dominant GPU memory consumer. Current single-GPU KV layouts hit limits for large LLMs and force costly host-eviction. We must support two common deployment topologies: (1) data-parallel + tensor-parallel shards across a single node (multi-GPU NVLink/PCIe) and (2) pipeline-parallel across multiple nodes (inter-node RPC between stages). Requirements: - Maintain per-request prefix KV correctness across TP and PP boundaries. - Keep incremental append and KV lookup ops low-latency for streaming continuous-batching. - Avoid global synchronization that prevents high throughput batching. - Minimize additional GPU memory overhead (aux buffers) and reduce host staging. - Provide fallbacks to single-GPU KV layout when TP/PP config does not support sharding. Proposed design (summary): 1) Shard key/value tensors along the model hidden dimension for TP (head or per-dim split) and along sequence dimension for PP stage-internal KV pointers: - For TP: each GPU holds KV slices corresponding to its local weight shard. This reduces per-GPU memory roughly by TP factor. - For PP: each pipeline stage stores the KV for tokens produced/consumed within that stage; inter-stage transfers carry only the minimal meta-pointer and per-head reduced representations when possible. 2) Logical KV index layer: Introduce a thin logical mapping layer that translates (request_id, layer, head, seq_pos) -> (device_id, device_offset, local_slice_shape). This mapping is computed once per batch and cached for continuous batches; mapping updates only when model partitioning or batch shape changes. 3) Continuous batching integration: - Allocate KV slabs per-device sized to predicted max-batch-length for the current batching window. - Use a compact slab allocator to pack multiple requests' KVs and enable fast append without moving existing entries. - When a token requires attention to keys on another device (TP/PP boundary), issue an async peer-to-peer fetch for the relevant local slice; overlap with computation and avoid blocking the main compute stream. 4) Communication primitives: - Use NCCL P2P for same-node GPU transfers (TP case). - For PP across nodes, use a lightweight RPC that sends compressed KV deltas (quantized 8-bit or chunked fp16) and rehydrates on destination GPU. - Add a selective compression pass for long contexts: compress older prefixes where precision loss is least damaging. 5) Failure and fallback modes: - If P2P unavailable, gracefully fall back to host-staged transfers. - If KV mapping conflicts or memory fragmentation detected, fall back to single-GPU global KV copy for the affected requests and mark metrics. Trade-offs discussed: - Sharding along hidden dims reduces memory but increases cross-device attention communication (more fine-grained fetches); this is acceptable for models where TP is already used for matmul sharding. - Sequence-shard (per-seq partition) simplifies PP cross-stage transfer but complicates attention computations that need full sequence history; therefore adopt hybrid approach per stage. - Compression reduces memory but can introduce slight quality degradation; make it opt-in with thresholds. Implementation plan (milestones): - M1 (Spike, 1 week): Microbenchmarks of hidden-dim sharding latency vs host-staging (scripts in /bench/kv-shard-spike). - M2 (Runtime prototype, 2 sprints): Implement logical KV index, per-device slab allocator, and async P2P fetch path; expose config flags. - M3 (PP support, 1 sprint): Add RPC path with compressed deltas for inter-node PP. - M4 (QA & rollout, 1 sprint): Stress tests, long-context evals, and gradual rollout behind a feature flag. Observability and safety: - Add metrics: per-request extra-latency (KV fetch), p2p-fallback-rate, compression-ratio, fragmentation-rate, and memory-savings. - Surface per-route diagnostics in Console (kv-shard.enabled, mode, fallback-reason). Benchmarks: Draft bench plan attached: - End-to-end streaming latency for 1/2/4/8 TP shards at 2k/8k/32k contexts. - Throughput under continuous batching (micro-batcher sizes 1-256). - Quality regression tests: LM perplexity and instruction-following evals on compressed prefixes. Artifacts: - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Multi-GPU+KV+Sharding (WIP) - Spike repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-shard-spike (branch: tp-pp-prototype) - Draft PR placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2561 (WIP) Acceptance criteria: - <10% throughput regression vs current single-GPU KV for same aggregate GPU memory use on standard workloads. - No correctness regressions on per-request attention windows at 32k context. - Feature flag enabled rollout with graceful fallback and telemetry. Rollout plan: Start with internal dogfood with synthetic workloads and staff tenants, then enable for a small set of Dedicated customers, monitor p2p-fallback-rate and memory savings, then broad rollout.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha Patel: Kickoff note. Spike approved for 5 dedicated GPU hours. Focus on TP hidden-dim sharding first; PP plan will piggyback on RPC layer.

2026-03-11 - Daniel Kim: Ran spike microbenchmarks. Observations: NCCL P2P latency for 4 GPUs is ~12-18us for 128B slices; host roundtrip is ~250us. Initial numbers justify P2P-first approach. Uploaded results: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-shard-spike-2026-03-11
2026-03-12 - Review (SRE): Raised concern about fragmentation for long-running servers. Suggested adding compact/defrag pass and eviction heuristics. Added to tasks.
2026-03-12 - UX (Product): Requesting Console flags and per-route breakdowns. We'll add UI ticket in product-management backlog.

2026-03-13 - Daniel Kim: Implemented logical KV index prototype (branch: feature/ENG-7420-kv-index). Preliminary tests show 1.3x memory reduction on 8k context for a 2-way TP split. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2561
2026-03-13 - Asha Patel: Decision: Compression default off. Enable heuristics to compress prefixes longer than 16k and allow customer opt-in. Added to acceptance criteria.
